findings.reason: The protected source takes the canonical repeated-draw tradeoff: materialize one value per node once, then use random.choice for independent constant-time draws. It preserves duplicate-node weighting, defines the required local ListNode model explicitly, and keeps the adapter minimal. No candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 382 and its Python Solution.getRandom surface. The Reference preserves uniform probability over nodes, independent calls, the nonempty linked-list contract, the app-local draw count, the source example and linked-list illustration, all three constraints, and both unknown-length constant-space follow-up prompts.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064659687. Its one-time traversal, occurrence-preserving value array, and random choice are exactly the protected app-local Solution algorithm; the local ListNode definition and multi-draw solve wrapper are required offline adapters.

The legal 32, 96, and 256 tiers use equal list length and draw count, span 8x, and distinguish one-time materialization from a full traversal per draw. The current source passes all 10 executions at -0.02 relative growth and 1.00x; correct reservoir sampling per draw passes every benchmark output but fails only scaling at +1.28 and 372.47x.

The Approach accurately derives uniform selection from dense occurrence positions, explains why duplicate values retain their node-weighted probability, separates semantic validation from statistical proof, states O(n + draws) time and O(n) space, and identifies reservoir sampling as the constant-space follow-up tradeoff.

The hash-bound public Reference remains source-fidelity verified, including the class contract, uniform independent selections, the sole source example, an equivalent accessible list diagram, all three constraints, and both source-native follow-up questions.
